title: Protect development environments and identities: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: How can a developer build and support software with reproducible environments while keeping identities, repositories, and secrets appropriately separated?
focalInsight: Supported tools/libraries, hardened IDE, organization identity, repository protection, managed secrets, and reproducible configuration.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Programming Languages
nodes.definition: Languages and supported versions chosen for maintainability, secure features, tool support, and known lifecycle ownership.
nodes.decision: Select maintained language/runtime versions with security support and an accountable upgrade plan.
nodes.failureExample: A team can write careful code yet inherit risk from an unsupported runtime with no security fixes.
nodes.detail: Languages and supported versions chosen for maintainability, secure features, tool support, and known lifecycle ownership.

nodes.label: Libraries
nodes.definition: Reusable code components and frameworks included in an application to supply functions or security-relevant behavior.
nodes.decision: Choose maintained, reviewed libraries with known provenance, licensing, version constraints, and vulnerability response ownership.
nodes.failureExample: Copying an unvetted package or stale library can import an exploitable dependency into every build.
nodes.detail: Reusable code components and frameworks included in an application to supply functions or security-relevant behavior.

nodes.label: Ide
nodes.definition: An integrated development environment and its extensions, settings, credentials, and plugins used to create and maintain code.
nodes.decision: Harden and manage IDEs/extensions, keep them updated, and prevent privileged credentials or unreviewed plugins from widening the workstation attack surface.
nodes.failureExample: A malicious IDE extension can read source and developer tokens before code ever reaches the repository.
nodes.detail: An integrated development environment and its extensions, settings, credentials, and plugins used to create and maintain code.

nodes.label: Source Control
nodes.definition: A system that records controlled versions, branches, changes, authorship, and merge history for source and related artifacts.
nodes.decision: Require authenticated changes, protected critical branches, review/approval rules, and traceable links from change to revision.
nodes.failureExample: Direct unreviewed pushes to the release branch can introduce a backdoor with no accountable review.
nodes.detail: A system that records controlled versions, branches, changes, authorship, and merge history for source and related artifacts.

nodes.label: Secrets Management
nodes.definition: Controlled storage, retrieval, rotation, revocation, and audit of credentials, keys, tokens, and other sensitive values.
nodes.decision: Keep secrets out of code/logs, use scoped identities to retrieve them, rotate on exposure or lifecycle events, and record references rather than values.
nodes.failureExample: A production token in a repository can be cloned, cached, and reused long after the code change is removed.
nodes.detail: Controlled storage, retrieval, rotation, revocation, and audit of credentials, keys, tokens, and other sensitive values.

nodes.label: Repository Security
nodes.definition: Protection of source/artifact repositories through access control, branch protection, review, integrity, availability, and audit.
nodes.decision: Apply least privilege, review rules, protected release paths, backup/availability, and alerting for sensitive changes.
nodes.failureExample: A repository administrator’s unmonitored account can alter both source history and release configuration.
nodes.detail: Protection of source/artifact repositories through access control, branch protection, review, integrity, availability, and audit.

nodes.label: Developer Identity
nodes.definition: An attributable, managed identity used by a developer or automation to access development resources with defined privileges.
nodes.decision: Use strong authentication, least privilege, separate personal/organizational and environment identities, and timely revocation.
nodes.failureExample: Shared developer accounts erase accountability and make compromise containment uncertain.
nodes.detail: An attributable, managed identity used by a developer or automation to access development resources with defined privileges.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: How can a developer build and support software with reproducible environments while keeping identities, repositories, and secrets appropriately separated?
learningContract.misconception: A capable developer account should work everywhere, and recording a secret in configuration improves reproducibility.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Supported tools/libraries, hardened IDE, organization identity, repository protection, managed secrets, and reproducible configuration.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not prescribe an IDE, language, secret product, token lifetime, or branch naming convention.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: A developer must troubleshoot production. Which identity, secret-access path, and audit/expiry evidence are appropriate?
